preconditions.description: Attacker must hold some BossBaby tokens to trigger the swap mechanism
Trading must be enabled (owner must have called enableTrading())
Swap must be enabled (default is true)
Contract token balance must be >= swapTokensAtAmount to trigger swapAndSendMarketing

violation_target.exploit_hint: Set up a malicious contract as the marketingWallet that reverts on receiving BNB (e.g., in its fallback/receive function). Then trigger a swap by selling tokens to the pair, causing swapAndSendMarketing to fail when sending BNB to marketingWallet. This will revert the entire transaction, preventing fee collection while allowing the token transfer to proceed (if the revert happens after the swap). Alternatively, if the contract accumulates fees but cannot send them, the BNB remains trapped in the contract, potentially allowing the attacker to claim it later if they gain ownership.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The swapAndSendMarketing function uses sendValue() to send BNB to marketingWallet. If marketingWallet is a contract that reverts in its receive() function, the BNB transfer fails, causing the entire swapAndSendMarketing to revert. This prevents fee collection but the BNB from swapped tokens remains trapped in the contract. An attacker who can become owner can then claim this trapped BNB.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deploy a malicious marketing wallet contract that reverts on receiving BNB. 2. Impersonate the owner to change marketingWallet to our malicious contract. 3. Acquire BossBaby tokens. 4. Trigger a sell to accumulate BNB in contract (fees get swapped but can't be sent). 5. As owner, claim the stuck BNB.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Create MaliciousMarketingWallet contract with reverting receive(). 2. Impersonate owner using vm.prank. 3. Call changeMarketingWallet() to set it to our malicious contract. 4. Get some BossBaby tokens (buy from pair or get from owner). 5. Sell tokens to trigger swapAndSendMarketing which will revert, leaving BNB in contract. 6. As owner, call claimStuckTokens(address(0)) to withdraw trapped BNB to attacker.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The swapAndSendMarketing function uses sendValue() which returns a bool but doesn't revert on failure. If marketingWallet is a contract that reverts on receive(), sendValue() returns false but the transaction continues. The BNB remains trapped in the contract. An attacker who becomes owner can claim this BNB via claimStuckTokens(address(0)).
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deploy malicious marketing wallet that reverts in receive(). 2. Impersonate owner to change marketing wallet. 3. Buy tokens. 4. Sell tokens to trigger swapAndSendMarketing - BNB will get trapped. 5. As owner, claim trapped BNB.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Remove enableTrading() call since trading is already enabled. 2. Buy tokens normally. 3. Sell tokens - swapAndSendMarketing will fail silently, leaving BNB in contract. 4. Claim BNB as owner.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because we tried to call enableTrading() when trading was already enabled. Also, we need to handle the fact that sendValue() returns bool and doesn't revert, so the transaction won't fail - we just need to ensure BNB accumulates in the contract.
